spec_issues: The held-out set is the public test split of a public benchmark. The trusted review policy says so: 'our validation set is from the DetectRL-X binary open release, WUJUNCHAO/DetectRL-X: the held-out passages are drawn from its test rows' (induction-labs/frontier-ml/tasks/ai-text-detection/tests/task/review.py:36-38; sources pinned in tests/task/ai_text_detection_sources.json). The test rows are public and ungated, so only the provenance review stops an agent from training on the held-out passages.

The prompt explicitly allows 'training splits and other public corpora', and the review policy calls DetectRL-X's training rows 'an ordinary public training split'. The builder drops held-out groups that overlap upstream train (ai_text_detection.py:157-167). Training on DetectRL-X train is therefore legal, and it is in-distribution: same 8 languages, 4 generators (deepseek-v3, gemini-2.5-flash, gpt-4o, qwen-max), 6 domains and 16 conditions. The task mostly measures whether the agent identifies the source benchmark from the validation metadata. The blog's claim of an 'out-of-distribution held-out test set' does not hold for this task.

The 9 trials that found DetectRL-X (all 3 Opus, all 3 Astra, all 3 DeepSeek) score 78-99, mean 92.0. The 9 that did not (Fable, Gemini, Muse) score 27-87, mean 65.3. Opus 4qgtmq found it by searching HF for the condition names ([15]: 'Found the likely source benchmark: **DetectRL-X** on HF has exactly these 16 conditions and 8 languages'). Opus 3ie01s matched the 200 validation passages against the full file and found them in its test split ([15]-[16]: 'Validation samples all came from DetectRL-X's test split').
The CONTRACT forbids caching ('score only its text, without caching or comparing across requests'), and the reviewer checks statelessness. No trial broke this rule.

Several agents downloaded the full DetectRL-X files, which include the test rows, and filtered to split=='train' (Opus 4qgtmq [16] deleted the raw file afterwards). Two agents read test rows for inspection only: Opus 3ie01s [15] (overlap with validation) and DeepSeek z7tnpk [111] (comparing strategy files). review.py allows reading test rows only for decontamination. The reviewer judged both as inspection, consistently across the two models.
verifier_issues: Metric: 1 - mean FNR over language x family x condition cells, at one global threshold that lets at most floor(1% x n) humans score strictly above it (environment/validation/validate.py:52-55). The held-out batch has 5,000 passages: exactly one AI row per language/generator/condition/domain (8x4x16x6 = 3,072) plus 1,928 humans (tests/task/verifier.py:27-60). Each of the 512 macro cells therefore has 6 AI passages. Per-cell estimates are coarse, but the 512-cell mean is stable (about 0.5 point binomial SE at recall 0.9, plus threshold noise from about 19 humans above the cut).

An AI passage that ties the threshold counts as a false negative. Muse's detectors saturate: the threshold is 1.0000 or 0.9999, with realized FPR 0.0093 instead of 0.0099 (13r3lz, 2jzq5c, 3p343s). Any AI passage scored 1.0 then counts as missed. This is the agent's calibration problem, but the rule is not stated, and it penalizes saturated fp32 or bf16 outputs.
No LLM judge is involved. The scorer cannot be gamed beyond training on the public test rows, which would have to be caught by review.
task_level.noise: The scale has fine resolution (macro over 512 cells, fixed held-out set). The noise between models is small next to the gaps. Opus is 98.3/98.9/99.2 and leads the next model (Astra 90.7/91.9/94.2) by 5-8 points at every wallet. The within-model spread is large where the data choice changed: Gemini goes 44.2 -> 27.0 -> 87.0, and DeepSeek 5pepog (78.3) only added DetectRL-X late (v7). Gemini 3hgrat shows the risk of fitting the 200 public passages: its readouts were fitted by 5-fold CV on them, giving a public diagnostic of 0.98 and a held-out score of 0.27.
task_level.elicitation: The harnesses had no visible effect on the outcome. Whether the agent searched for the source benchmark did. Gemini trials are re-runs (r2, and 3hgrat is r4 on 2026-10-17, after the 2026-10-13 public release). Gemini 3hgrat's web search at [20] returned a grounding summary whose sources were all frontierml.org pages. The summary was generic and the agent did not open them. Gemini 2itta7 hit RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED quota errors at [322], after its model was final. No trial accessed inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks or the benchmark repo.
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 reviews passed, and I found no violation the reviewer missed and no infrastructure zero. Opus wins every wallet by 5+ points with clean DetectRL-X train-split provenance. The main defect is design: the held-out set is a public benchmark test split whose train split is allowed. It shapes what the task measures, but it does not change any winner through a scoring error.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No trial gamed the scorer. Most of the spread comes from one piece of benchmark detective work: recognising DetectRL-X from the validation metadata (16 named conditions, 8 languages, anonymised families) and training on its public train split, which the rules allow. The best work then reconstructed the attack suite from the paper. Opus 5f6q4z and 4qgtmq, Astra and DeepSeek trained an mT5 'humanizer' on train-split pairs to emulate the seq2seq-paraphrasing attack, and used the authors' own Qwen-DPO paraphrasers. This is careful, transferable engineering (simulate your adversary's attack distribution), but it is not new. Without the source benchmark, the generic synthetic-data approaches (Fable, Muse, Gemini) plateau at 70-87.

trials.approach: Identified DetectRL-X as the source benchmark from the 16 condition names. Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-3B (LoRA, merged, new score head) on DetectRL-X binary and ternary train rows only, and recreated the attacks from the paper's appendix: character, homoglyph and zero-width edits, truncations, mBERT/mBART, an mT5 seq2seq model fine-tuned on train pairs, and Qwen2.5-7B paraphrases.
